title: This Machine Makes Ice You Can Actually Chew
summary:
Have you ever bitten into a piece of ice and felt like you might break a tooth? Ouch. Well, there's a special kind of ice that's soft and easy to chew. It's called nugget ice, and it's made of tiny, airy flakes packed together. It's crunchy like a snowball, and it melts slowly. That means your drink stays cold, and the ice soaks up the flavor of whatever you're drinking. Some people call it "Sonic ice" because a fast-food place called Sonic made it famous.

Now you can make nugget ice right on your kitchen counter. These machines are called countertop nugget ice makers. They're a bit like a mini fridge, but they churn out ice all day. One machine, the GE Profile Opal 2.0 Ultra, can make enough ice for a big party. It's about the size of two shoeboxes side by side. It can get noisy when it's working — about as loud as a loud refrigerator. But when it's just keeping ice cold, it's almost silent.

Another machine, the Euhomy Smart, is smaller and can make 40 pounds of ice per day. That's like 40 bags of ice from the store! It makes its first batch in under 10 minutes. The Gevi 2.0 has a big basket that holds almost 5 pounds of ice. Its door opens wide, so you can scoop ice easily. These machines usually start around $400. That's a lot of money, but for ice lovers, it might be worth it. No more ice trays!
why_it_matters: Understanding how a machine turns water into soft ice can help you figure out the gadgets in your own kitchen, and maybe inspire you to invent something useful for your family.

background_read: Soft, chewable ice has been served for many years in restaurants and hospitals, because it is gentle on your mouth.
A company called Scotsman invented nugget ice, and Sonic (a drive-in fast-food chain in the United States that is famous for its drinks) helped make it popular.
GE (a big American company that makes fridges, ovens, and other home appliances) is one of the companies now making these ice machines for home kitchens.
Article_Structure: WHO: Nugget ice fans, and the companies GE, Euhomy, and Gevi that make countertop nugget ice makers.
WHAT: Small kitchen machines that make soft, chewable nugget ice at home, all day long.
WHERE: On kitchen counters — the machines are about the size of two shoeboxes side by side, and nugget ice became famous at a fast-food place called Sonic.
WHY: Nugget ice is crunchy, melts slowly, and soaks up the flavor of drinks, so people want it at home — and these machines mean no more ice trays.

perspectives.description: People who love chewing ice and want cold drinks that keep their flavor say these machines are worth the money.
Some people think around $400 is a lot to pay for ice when you can buy a bag of ice or use an ice tray for almost nothing.
A machine that is noisy and takes up counter space might not be welcome in a small kitchen, even if the ice tastes great.
